reply.text:
Good on you for bringing him in. At 11, the goal is learning to move well and enjoying it, not loading the bar. Light weights or bodyweight, a few sets of 8 to 12 clean reps, and form that someone is watching every rep. Think squats, push-ups, rows, planks and carries, and let him add weight slowly when the technique is clean.

Two or three short sessions a week is plenty, and he doesn't need to match your pace or your lifts. Before he starts a program, it's worth a quick word with his doctor or pediatrician, and a coach who works with kids is a good second set of eyes on his form.

I can't build a program for an 11-year-old in the app, since it's set up for adult athletes. I can help with your own training, or with how to structure your sessions so he can join in on the easy parts, like warm-ups and bodyweight work.
